title: Minimum Project Completion Time
statement: You are scheduling n tasks labeled 1 to n. You are given a list time of length n where time[i-1] is the number of hours task i takes to run, and a list relations of pairs [a, b], each meaning task a must fully finish before task b may start. Any number of tasks may run at the same time, and a task starts the instant all of its prerequisites have finished. Define finish[v] = time[v] + max(finish[u]) over all prerequisites u of v (with the max being 0 when v has no prerequisites). Return the minimum number of hours to finish every task, which equals max(finish[v]) over all v. If the relations contain a dependency cycle so that some task can never start, return -1. Return a single integer.
hints: A task can only start once all of its prerequisites are done, so you must process tasks in an order that respects every 'must finish before' relation; the twist is that each task carries a weight (its duration) rather than just counting levels.
Process tasks in topological order and carry a finish[] array: a task's finish time is its own duration plus the largest finish time among its prerequisites (the critical path into it).

Use Kahn's algorithm. When you pop task u, add time[u-1] to finish[u], then for each successor w relax finish[w] = max(finish[w], finish[u]) before decrementing its in-degree. The answer is max over all finish[v], or -1 if fewer than n tasks were ever processed (a cycle).
